anti_goal_violations.anti_goal: Persistence stays scoped. Fetching/recording/exposure is always an explicit operator act; page loads and Foundry reads never record market data. `GET /research/desk/micro/foundry` and every page-load GET are read-only and never compute/evaluate a candidate or trigger the exhaust runner.
anti_goal_violations.evidence: The Foundry read surface performs a filesystem WRITE on every page load. micro_routes.get_foundry() calls foundry_runner.read_exhaust_progress per request, which runs a live single-flight probe (foundry_runner.py:250-254); SingleFlightLock.acquire (foundry_runner.py:197-201) does path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True) then open(path, 'w') BEFORE the try, so a GET creates/truncates apps/backend/.data/foundry/foundry_exhaust_runner.lock. Evaluator read the code directly in iter-6; iter-6 audit finding B5 confirmed the real lock file's mtime tracks the QA browser pass, not the CLI run. Named consequences: a GET holding LOCK_EX for microseconds can make a concurrent exhaust-CLI invocation raise ConcurrentRunnerRefused; an unwritable Foundry directory now 500s a surface that was previously write-free; errno.EACCES is mapped to ConcurrentRunnerRefused so a permissions failure would be reported to the operator as 'Running - lock held by another invocation'. SCORED AS A LITERAL-READING VIOLATION and disclosed as such: the rail's operative intent is INTACT - no market data is recorded, no candidate is computed or evaluated, and the exhaust runner is not triggered - only the words 'are read-only' are contradicted. MINOR, never critical (no secret, paid dependency, license breach, backdoor, or fabricated data, and not goal.md's own named critical violation). UNFIXABLE INSIDE THIS ERA: the fix site is read_exhaust_progress/SingleFlightLock inside foundry_runner.py, a freeze-set member whose sha256 is pinned in the one-way epoch_open ledger row - so this is an owner disposition decision, not an iteration task. | ITER-7 UPDATE (status UNCHANGED, still BLOCKING, OWNER-ONLY): explicitly out of scope this iteration and re-confirmed unchanged. Auditor finding B4 re-read the path rather than trusting the handoff and reached the same conclusion; the evaluator confirms foundry_runner.py is one of the 59 freeze-set entries whose sha256 it recomputed as byte-identical, so no legal fix exists without owner sanction to break the seal. Mitigating fact the auditor established and the evaluator re-verified via the store-scope guard: the lock file's target resolves to apps/backend/.data/foundry/, which is gitignored and is NOT one of the guard's protected paths - reports/qa/goal-hypothesis-foundry-iter-7-store-scope-guard.md is CLEAN with all 11395 protected files byte-identical before and after this run.

owner_disposition.ruling: Owner ruling 2026-08-27: preserve the first-read seal rather than edit the sealed runner to remove the GET-side lock probe. The lock-file creation/truncation is a real, disclosed minor violation of the literal "read-only" wording, but it mutates no scientific state, market data, candidate result, trial ledger or protected evidence. It is non-blocking for this completed Foundry epoch and must be corrected in a future named Foundry revision before this architecture is reused.
